# Catalog pipeline delivery plan

A rights-governed, evidence-backed ingestion and immutable publishing service for the whole AI research ecosystem.

## Preparation and execution boundary

Prepared local scope baseline. No GitHub issues or Project resources are established by this file. Runtime implementation remains unstarted; GitHub owns live status and assignees after publication.

The baseline contains **81 intended native issues**: one Program, 16 Epics and 64 independently reviewable Work Packages. Their implementation detail is 192 stable checklist Tasks and 384 Subtasks.

Program -> native epic sub-issues -> native independently reviewable work-package sub-issues -> stable checklist tasks -> stable checklist subtasks. Promote a task to a native issue only for an independently accepted owner or review boundary.

GitHub Assignees are authoritative. Proposed role descriptions do not assign people or teams. A work package needs an accepted actual assignee before Ready.

Planning JSON owns scope, acceptance and traceability. GitHub owns current execution state. Reconciliation must preserve live assignees, existing comments, approved decisions and progress.

The [generated issue payloads](../planning/github-issue-payloads.json) and [individual issue bodies](../planning/issues/CP.md) are prepared inputs. They contain no verified GitHub issue IDs or Project identity. The [setup procedure](PROJECT_SETUP.md) requires authenticated discovery, reconciliation and readback.

## Program acceptance

- Two bounded eligible domain pilots demonstrate source-to-review-to-publication-to-consumer delivery with exact artifact and rights evidence.
- Mandatory refusal, conflict, correction, withdrawal and rollback cases pass at real supported boundaries.
- Affected research and consumer owners accept the exact contract, evidence and publication handoffs.
- The released scope has independent readiness review, accepted operational ownership and verified recovery evidence.

## Decisions and release impact

Role names identify needed decision authority; the blank actual approver lists do not imply anyone has accepted a new duty. Existing accepted boundaries are cited upstream rather than re-approved locally.

### D-001: Dedicated catalog pipeline delivery boundary

**Status:** Established by current mission. **Decision role:** Organization administrator and pipeline maintainer.

One public repository and dedicated organization Project; pipeline owns shared ingestion/review/publication, research owns policy/evidence and consumers own UI/service acceptance.

Options and tradeoffs:

- **Dedicated shared pipeline** — One delivery boundary for reusable ETL/review/publication; requires separate maintenance and handoff ownership.
- **Keep machinery inside one consumer** — Lower repository count but couples other clients and broad research to one app release cycle.

Consequences:

- Research and client ownership remain unchanged; new service deployment is not implied.

Affected release gates: Foundation.

Packages: [CP-01.01](../planning/issues/CP-01.01.md), [CP-01.03](../planning/issues/CP-01.03.md).

User mission; actual GitHub setup readback still required.

References:

- https://github.com/Pick-Your-AI/pick-your-ai-research/issues/509

### D-002: Preserve canonical research and frozen contracts

**Status:** Existing accepted boundary. **Decision role:** Canonical research contract reviewer with affected consumers.

Do not modify frozen builder v1 or reopen completed research criteria; route new semantics through research #40.

Options and tradeoffs:

- **Preserve frozen v1 and version extensions separately** — Retains consumer compatibility and original hashes; new semantics need an explicit adoption packet.
- **Mutate existing v1 in place** — Would change accepted wire meaning and break reproducibility; excluded by existing governance.

Consequences:

- Broad catalog data may be withheld from builder projections until an accepted compatible mapping exists.

Affected release gates: Foundation, Bounded Pilot.

Packages: [CP-02.01](../planning/issues/CP-02.01.md), [CP-02.02](../planning/issues/CP-02.02.md), [CP-02.03](../planning/issues/CP-02.03.md).

Existing research contract process, not new pipeline authority.

References:

- https://github.com/Pick-Your-AI/pick-your-ai-research/issues/40

### D-003: Deny missing or insufficient source-use permission

**Status:** Existing accepted boundary. **Decision role:** Canonical source-rights decision maker with research #41/#60 authority.

Retrieval/display/cache/export/redistribution are separate and scoped per source, field, product and use; current GPUs.io API/display/export exclusion remains.

Options and tradeoffs:

- **Evaluate explicit material/product/use decisions** — Supports traceable grants and denials; requires field-level provenance and ongoing terms review.
- **Infer permission from public availability or a permissive fragment** — Reduces manual review but cannot establish eligible reuse; excluded by the accepted handoff.

Consequences:

- Unknown, expired, revoked and excluded uses remain blocked even if schema validation succeeds.

Affected release gates: Foundation, Bounded Pilot, Production.

Packages: [CP-03.01](../planning/issues/CP-03.01.md), [CP-03.02](../planning/issues/CP-03.02.md), [CP-03.03](../planning/issues/CP-03.03.md).

Source owner and research #60/#41 decisions are required for new uses.

References:

- https://github.com/Pick-Your-AI/pick-your-ai-research/blob/main/docs/PUBLICATION_ELIGIBILITY_HANDOFF.md

### D-004: Keep one canonical planner API

**Status:** Existing accepted boundary. **Decision role:** Existing shared-service owner/coordinator and affected consumer reviewers.

Retain the accepted TypeScript/Node API and PostgreSQL on Render with website services/planner-api source placement; pipeline delivers exact approved bytes and handoff receipts, not a competing backend.

Options and tradeoffs:

- **Feed the selected canonical planner API** — Reuses accepted authority and transaction model; requires exact byte and activation handoffs.
- **Create a separate planner API in this repository** — Duplicates build/auth/evaluation ownership and compatibility state; excluded from current scope.

Consequences:

- Pipeline staging and workers must remain distinct from the canonical consumer service authority.

Affected release gates: Foundation, Bounded Pilot, Beta.

Packages: [CP-01.04](../planning/issues/CP-01.04.md), [CP-10.04](../planning/issues/CP-10.04.md), [CP-12.01](../planning/issues/CP-12.01.md), [CP-14.01](../planning/issues/CP-14.01.md).

Existing service owner/coordinator; unfilled operating gates are not auto-assigned.

References:

- https://github.com/Pick-Your-AI/pick-your-ai-android/blob/main/docs/SERVICE_BASELINE.md

### D-005: Synthetic-only repository bootstrap

**Status:** Established by current mission. **Decision role:** Pipeline maintainer and bootstrap reviewer.

Initial fixtures are fictional and labeled; bootstrap performs no acquisition, paid provisioning or production deployment.

Options and tradeoffs:

- **Use labeled fictional fixtures only** — Enables repeatable validation without implying permissions; cannot establish real source capability.
- **Import existing research proposals as live seed data** — Could appear more realistic but lacks blanket publication clearance; excluded from bootstrap.

Consequences:

- Synthetic grants, reviews and prices cannot satisfy a production release gate.

Affected release gates: Foundation.

Packages: [CP-15.01](../planning/issues/CP-15.01.md), [CP-15.02](../planning/issues/CP-15.02.md).

User mission and repository bootstrap gate.

### D-006: Native hierarchy with checklist execution detail

**Status:** Proposed implementation convention. **Decision role:** Pipeline maintainer and organization Project administrator.

Use Program > Epic > Work Package native issues, stable checklist Tasks/Subtasks, and promote tasks when an independent owner/review boundary is accepted.

Options and tradeoffs:

- **Native Program/Epic/WP with checklist tasks** — Matches established planning precedent and keeps independent outcomes navigable; later task promotion needs reconciliation.
- **Make every step a native issue** — Creates more independently assignable records but adds coordination overhead and duplicates checklist progress.

Consequences:

- Stable task IDs survive promotion; native hierarchy and blockers are verified independently.

Affected release gates: Foundation.

Packages: [CP-01.03](../planning/issues/CP-01.03.md).

Follows inspected leaderboard convention; actual native readback required.

References:

- https://github.com/Pick-Your-AI/pick-your-ai-leaderboard/blob/main/planning/README.md

### D-007: Real ownership and independent review

**Status:** Existing accepted boundary. **Decision role:** Authorized organization administrator and independent review coordinator.

Live native GitHub Assignees express accepted ownership; team-based access and independent approval follow organization policy.

Options and tradeoffs:

- **Use native Assignees and verified team permissions** — Preserves actual accepted ownership and least privilege; vacancies remain visible.
- **Infer ownership from historical roles or an Owner field** — Looks complete but invents assignments and creates conflicting authority; excluded.

Consequences:

- Unfilled owner or independent-review roles can block readiness while useful local work continues.

Affected release gates: Foundation, Production.

Packages: [CP-01.02](../planning/issues/CP-01.02.md), [CP-08.02](../planning/issues/CP-08.02.md).

No task assignee, on-call role or team member is invented.

References:

- https://github.com/Pick-Your-AI/.github/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md

### D-008: Multi-domain pipeline schema separated from builder v1

**Status:** Proposed technical design. **Decision role:** Research taxonomy/contract reviewer and pipeline schema maintainer.

Use an independently versioned envelope and typed graph for models, offers, hardware, datasets, apps, papers, tools, use cases and guides; project only compatible subsets.

Options and tradeoffs:

- **Separate typed pipeline envelope with reviewed projections** — Supports diverse resource kinds; requires mapping/version governance.
- **Force all resources into frozen builder component kinds** — Reduces schemas but loses domain meaning and silently extends accepted v1; excluded.

Consequences:

- Entity types remain extensible through accepted versions; unsupported projections are withheld.

Affected release gates: Foundation, Expansion.

Packages: [CP-02.01](../planning/issues/CP-02.01.md), [CP-02.04](../planning/issues/CP-02.04.md).

Research contract and affected receiving-owner review at implementation.

References:

- https://github.com/Pick-Your-AI/pick-your-ai-research/issues/509

### D-009: First eligible source and pilot selection

**Status:** Awaiting decision. **Decision role:** Relevant domain owner, source-rights decision maker and website receiving owner.

Select one model/provider and one hardware/runtime or tool pilot only after exact source-use scope and required fields are accepted.

Options and tradeoffs:

- **Choose existing rights-eligible structured metadata** — Offers a bounded reproducible pilot with explicit field restrictions; may omit desired prices or capabilities.
- **Request a new source/use decision before selecting the pilot** — Can expand coverage but delays live intake until accepted evidence exists.

Consequences:

- No complete existing research catalog or pricebook is presumed cleared; two distinct domain pilots are still required.

Affected release gates: Bounded Pilot.

Packages: [CP-04.02](../planning/issues/CP-04.02.md), [CP-16.01](../planning/issues/CP-16.01.md), [CP-16.02](../planning/issues/CP-16.02.md).

No complete current research catalog/pricebook is presumed cleared.

References:

- https://github.com/Pick-Your-AI/pick-your-ai-research/blob/main/docs/PUBLICATION_ELIGIBILITY_HANDOFF.md

### D-010: Pipeline worker runtime and durable execution placement

**Status:** Awaiting decision. **Decision role:** Pipeline technical maintainer with shared-service coordinator and operating owner.

Select only pipeline-owned runtime, scheduling and staging choices; preserve accepted canonical server/storage authority and justify any new large-object store.

Options and tradeoffs:

- **Small durable worker/staging layer integrated with accepted service** — Limits duplicated infrastructure; capacity must be measured.
- **Add independent queue/object-store services after measured need** — Can improve scale and isolation but adds cost, custody and restore complexity.

Consequences:

- No new paid resource or object store is created by naming an architecture; deployment needs accepted custody and budgets.

Affected release gates: Foundation, Bounded Pilot, Beta.

Packages: [CP-01.04](../planning/issues/CP-01.04.md), [CP-14.01](../planning/issues/CP-14.01.md), [CP-14.02](../planning/issues/CP-14.02.md).

Requires actual workload, owner, cost and recovery evidence before deployment.

References:

- https://github.com/Pick-Your-AI/pick-your-ai-android/blob/main/docs/SERVICE_BASELINE.md

### D-011: Signing and release custody

**Status:** Awaiting decision. **Decision role:** Release custodian and independent security reviewer.

Define signer identity, key custody, rotation and recovery before any production-signed artifact; no real keys belong in bootstrap.

Options and tradeoffs:

- **Short-lived workload signing identity** — Reduces static-key custody but needs a supported verification and identity policy.
- **Managed signing key with explicit custody and rotation** — Can fit existing infrastructure but requires recovery, access and compromise procedures.

Consequences:

- No production signing or acceptance claim until selected identity, verification and recovery are proven.

Affected release gates: Bounded Pilot, Production.

Packages: [CP-10.02](../planning/issues/CP-10.02.md), [CP-13.03](../planning/issues/CP-13.03.md).

Accepted release owner and independent reviewer required.

### D-012: Current pointer and public mirror compatibility

**Status:** Awaiting decision. **Decision role:** Research #40 contract reviewer and website/service receiving owner.

Frozen /v1 reads remain bearer-authenticated; current/latest aliases and anonymous public mirrors need separately accepted contracts and rights decisions.

Options and tradeoffs:

- **Use accepted authenticated v1 reads plus separately approved artifact channel** — Preserves frozen behavior and allows a narrow eligible public mirror with explicit rights.
- **Adopt a new version for anonymous discovery/current aliases** — Provides new semantics but needs coordinated schema, auth and consumer adoption.

Consequences:

- A static public file is not an implementation of the globally bearer-authenticated frozen API.

Affected release gates: Bounded Pilot, Beta.

Packages: [CP-10.04](../planning/issues/CP-10.04.md), [CP-12.01](../planning/issues/CP-12.01.md).

Research #40 and existing website #15–#18 consumer authority.

References:

- https://github.com/Pick-Your-AI/pick-your-ai-website/blob/main/docs/DATA_INTEGRATION.md
- https://github.com/Pick-Your-AI/pick-your-ai-android/blob/main/docs/SERVICE_BASELINE.md

### D-013: Freshness distinguishes historical and current-state facts

**Status:** Existing accepted boundary. **Decision role:** Research evidence/freshness and saved-build reviewers.

No universal TTL; capture/check/effective/publication times stay distinct, and a new snapshot alone does not invalidate saved builds.

Options and tradeoffs:

- **Separate immutable historical facts from current-state checks** — Preserves reproducibility; volatile facts still require source-aware refresh.
- **Apply one global TTL to all facts** — Simplifies scheduling but invents expiry semantics and can invalidate valid pinned builds; excluded.

Consequences:

- Capture/check/effective/publish timestamps and source-specific freshness status remain distinct.

Affected release gates: Bounded Pilot, Beta.

Packages: [CP-11.01](../planning/issues/CP-11.01.md), [CP-12.04](../planning/issues/CP-12.04.md).

Research #41/#42 semantics remain authoritative.

References:

- https://github.com/Pick-Your-AI/pick-your-ai-website/blob/main/docs/DATA_INTEGRATION.md

### D-014: Optional enrichment is proposal-only

**Status:** Deferred. **Decision role:** Pipeline maintainer, privacy/source-rights reviewers and cost authority.

Any AI enrichment needs separate provider privacy/rights/cost acceptance; it cannot approve rights, create facts or execute source instructions.

Options and tradeoffs:

- **Use deterministic enrichment and human review first** — Avoids provider disclosure/cost and makes transformations reproducible; some editorial work remains manual.
- **Add bounded AI proposals after explicit approval** — May reduce review effort but introduces model provenance, privacy, hallucination and cost risks.

Consequences:

- Generated content never approves rights, becomes independently verified evidence, or executes source instructions.

Affected release gates: Expansion.

Packages: [CP-08.04](../planning/issues/CP-08.04.md), [CP-13.02](../planning/issues/CP-13.02.md).

No paid inference use is authorized by bootstrap.

### D-015: Production operational acceptance

**Status:** Awaiting decision. **Decision role:** Accepted operating owner, recovery custodian and independent release reviewer.

Identify actual operating owner, recovery custodian, budgets and service objectives; local tests do not establish a live supported service.

Options and tradeoffs:

- **Release only after actual operational acceptance** — Establishes custody, recovery and supported limits; can delay launch.
- **Keep service in synthetic/staging qualification** — Allows independent testing while roles or budgets are missing; cannot be described as supported production.

Consequences:

- No person is assigned on-call responsibility by a role label or inherited client ownership.

Affected release gates: Production.

Packages: [CP-14.03](../planning/issues/CP-14.03.md), [CP-14.04](../planning/issues/CP-14.04.md), [CP-15.04](../planning/issues/CP-15.04.md).

Preserve existing unfilled service operating gates; do not assign volunteers by assumption.

References:

- https://github.com/Pick-Your-AI/pick-your-ai-android/blob/main/docs/SERVICE_BASELINE.md

### D-016: Expansion after two bounded pilots

**Status:** Proposed delivery sequencing. **Decision role:** Pipeline maintainer with each domain research owner and consumer reviewer.

Onboard datasets/apps/papers and other domains with their owning research corpus, rights assessment, measured maintenance cost and consumer acceptance.

Options and tradeoffs:

- **Expand after two qualified pilots using measured gates** — Tests reuse across distinct domains and bounds maintenance load; growth is deliberate.
- **Import all candidate domains immediately** — Increases apparent breadth but lacks rights, review capacity and accepted mappings; excluded from initial release.

Consequences:

- Coverage reports preserve explicit unknown denominators and do not claim completeness of all AI.

Affected release gates: Expansion.

Packages: [CP-16.01](../planning/issues/CP-16.01.md), [CP-16.02](../planning/issues/CP-16.02.md), [CP-16.03](../planning/issues/CP-16.03.md), [CP-16.04](../planning/issues/CP-16.04.md).

Pending future accepted pilot evidence; no new research repository assumed created.

References:

- https://github.com/Pick-Your-AI/pick-your-ai-research/issues/509

## Non-goals

- Production deployment by repository bootstrap
- Mutating frozen research contracts/v1
- Reopening completed T0–T6 research acceptance
- Duplicating website/mobile implementation or domain research
- Unapproved scraping, paid source subscriptions or external inference
- Treating sourced facts or synthetic fixtures as independently measured results
- Reinterpreting nonprofit sustainability research as technical energy data ownership
- Creating a competing evaluate/estimate/build/authentication service or overriding accepted website services/planner-api placement

## Bootstrap versus production

Repository and planning setup only, no production service or dataset.

Required bootstrap receipts:

- Public target repository identity and main commit
- Foundational files and synthetic fixture labels
- Successful local plan/schema/test/doc checks
- Actual organization Project identity, fields and saved-view readback
- Issue IDs, native hierarchy/dependency readback and complete Project membership
- Configured governance or exact access blockers

Forbidden completion inferences:

- Passing bootstrap CI implies a deployed service
- A research proposal or public source URL implies display/export permission
- A schema-valid benchmark implies independent reproduction
- A created issue or merged implementation PR implies all literal acceptance criteria are satisfied
- A new snapshot implies historical builds expired
